description: Local PostgreSQL and MinIO proof that an actual Docker worker container killed with SIGKILL after real object erasure but before database sweep or lease release is recovered by a separate replacement container after lease expiry, without parent-supplied account or object identifiers and without data resurrection.
requiredSequence: apply the canonical security migrations to local PostgreSQL and configure memory_app_login with NOINHERIT NOBYPASSRLS
host fixture creates one synthetic account, one upload ledger and at least one real versioned MinIO object, then begins deletion through memory_app_login and the canonical account-control service
container A receives only non-production database/object-store connection configuration and a signal-file path; it receives no account id, job id, authorization id or object key
container A verifies current_user is memory_app_login with rolsuper=false and rolbypassrls=false
container A claims deletion work at attempt 1, discovers the object key through the deletion-runtime ledger and erases a real object version
container A writes a fixed low-information ready signal and blocks before database sweep, completion or lease release
workflow sends docker kill --signal=KILL and verifies container A exits with code 137
host verifier proves database ledger remains, account remains deleting at attempt 1, object versions are zero and no replacement claim is available before lease expiry
after the five-second lease expires, container B starts with the same restricted connection configuration and no account/object identifiers
container B claims the same deletion work at attempt 2 and completes idempotent object erasure plus database sweep
container B exits zero after writing a fixed recovered signal
host final verifier proves pending/stuck backlog zero, all owned rows zero, deleted epoch-2 tombstone and zero object versions
abortCriteria: either worker container receives an account id, job id, authorization id or object key from the host
worker container is superuser or BYPASSRLS
container A does not erase a real object version before SIGKILL
container A exits normally or with a code other than 137
database ledger disappears before replacement-container recovery
a replacement claim is available before the killed container lease expires
container B does not prove attempt-2 reclaim
any owned row or object version survives or reappears
committed result contains a database URL, credential, account id, job id, authorization id, object key or container environment
limitations: Docker container kill and replacement do not prove physical host, VM, node, availability-zone or control-plane failure
five-second lease is test-only and not a production lease recommendation
local PostgreSQL 16 and MinIO are not production-equivalent dependencies
one killed container and one replacement container do not establish throughput, capacity or safe operating thresholds
